account: It is day 1, just after seven in the morning, and I am in my office after reading today's appointments and the secretary's notes. Today I have office business at eight, a grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea with my neighbour beside the east ferry landing at three, office again at sixteen-thirty, and an eighteen-hundred community gathering in the great hall before returning home at nineteen hundred. The gathering is an additional appointment requested by the innkeeper and approved yesterday. The innkeeper also wanted a private conversation with the secretary about catering; that seems consistent with preparing the gathering, though I do not know what they arranged. The only unusual report I have heard is my neighbour's vague mention of a bridge or port change overheard near the bakery. There is no identified source or confirmed proposal. The secretary found no such proposal in the office records checked, but that does not rule out records elsewhere, and intends to ask discreetly near the bakery. The accounts ledger's keeper and the normal location of incoming correspondence also remain unknown. These are unresolved administrative enquiries, not evidence of wrongdoing. I should return the three books to the appointments chest so the secretary can access them, then keep today's appointments and ask for any verified developments.
